notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text begins with DOI 10.1037/pspa0000032 and a KU Leuven repository SOURCE_URL; its title page names Less is More? Think Again! A Cognitive Fluency-Based More-Less Asymmetry in Comparative Communication, Vera Hoorens and Susanne Bruckmüller. It is a full primary research manuscript with Study 7 methods/results, references and figures, rather than an abstract or secondary report. The manuscript body has a subtitle variant (in Evaluations, Agreements, and Judgments of Truth). Title/authors and supplied DOI identify the assigned original work; journal publication metadata are not independently verified from this manuscript. No PDF was supplied. Only original n_o is assigned; other fields/sides are unassigned placeholders. The neutral locator identifies Study 7 and the warning manipulation on manuscript p. 32, but does not distinguish the three-condition omnibus agreement test, the planned contrast, or the warning-versus-standard-less post-hoc comparison. The reported participant total is 130, while the three printed condition counts sum to 119; the source does not reconcile this discrepancy or document exclusions. Consequently no unique critical-test analytic N can be assigned. Candidate sums are retained for parent field-scope review only. Candidate three-condition participant sum: 45 (more than) + 42 (less than with warning) + 32 (standard less than) = 119. Candidate warning-versus-standard-less participant sum: 42 + 32 = 74. Conditions are mutually exclusive between-subjects groups. These are candidate sums, not extracted analytic N. The methods report 130 participants; 130 - 119 = 11 is an unexplained reporting discrepancy, not a documented exclusion count. No N is derived from degrees of freedom. The omnibus reports F(2, 127) = 22.55 and partial eta-squared 0.26; the planned contrast reports t(127) = 5.25; the warning-versus-standard-less comparison reports p = .037. These identify candidate tests only and are not populated into unassigned statistic fields.
